intro: A rotation around a chosen point is a translation, a rotation around the origin and a translation back. Omitting either translation rotates around the wrong location.
task: Translate to a pivot, apply a 2D rotation in radians and translate back without modifying inputs.
requirements: points has shape (n,2), pivot has length two and angle is in radians. Positive angles rotate counterclockwise.
Return rotated points with the same shape. Translate by -pivot, apply x_new=cos(angle)*x-sin(angle)*y and y_new=sin(angle)*x+cos(angle)*y, then translate back.

Unless a requirement explicitly sets another range, numeric inputs are real and finite with magnitude at most 10000. Booleans are rejected except explicit boolean masks. Vectors have length 1..64 and matrix axes 1..64 unless specified otherwise. Leave inputs unchanged. Raise ValueError for invalid types, bounds, shapes or documented domain conditions.

examples.name: Quarter turn
examples.output:

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Subtract the pivot so the rotation can be performed around the origin.

hints.title: Build the result
hints.body: With row-stored points, multiply by the transpose of the usual column-vector rotation matrix.

explanation: A rotation around a chosen point is a translation, a rotation around the origin and a translation back. Omitting either translation rotates around the wrong location.
Rotations preserve distances and orientation. Applying the opposite angle should recover the original points, and a point equal to the pivot must remain fixed.
